title: Staff security engineer at Trestle Freight
context: Trestle Freight wants Mara, a security engineer who led identity modernization, to take ownership of its internal security platform. Both parties have already expressed interest. Work toward a written package each side can recommend.
private: The approved base range is $174–190k with an $18k signing pool. Mara is needed ahead of a July audit. The team wants weekly site visits for the first 12 weeks; you can substitute two three-day visits per month with travel covered. Incident coverage can be business-hours only if Mara trains the escalation partner. Decide how to allocate signing money versus start date.

Mara earns $185k and forfeits a $12k vest if she leaves before June 15. She can start June 1 if made whole, otherwise July 1. She lives four hours away and cannot commute weekly but can do grouped visits twice a month. She wants security architecture ownership and cannot be the sole after-hours responder. Negotiate the whole package and identify any dependency before recommending acceptance.

title: Six-month exhibit design contract at Hearth Museum
context: Hearth Museum has invited Ivo, an independent exhibition designer, to build an accessible traveling exhibit. They need an engagement agreement before a fabrication slot expires.
private: Ivo normally charges $900 per day. They can reserve 50 days, need milestone payments, and want permission to show photographs after the public opening. Two rounds of revisions are included; fabrication supervision is separate and requires advance dates. They would discount for a guaranteed block and rapid deposit. Put forward a package.

The grant pays at most $44k for design including two on-site installation days. The museum can pay a 20% deposit then pay at three milestones. It needs editable fabrication files and an accessible alternate layout. The sponsor restricts photos until a touring venue opens two months after launch. You can guarantee 46 days or pay a separate site travel allowance. Resolve scope, dates and rights.

title: Operations director succession at Caldera Water
context: Caldera Water and operations manager Dev are discussing succession to a retiring director. They want a transition plan that both can take to their boards.
private: Start an overlap by September; the incumbent remains director until January. You have $138k this year and $155k next year subject to an already approved appointment. The board can give Dev procurement authority up to $60k immediately but keeps personnel decisions until January. A training budget or temporary lodging can be offered, up to $8k total. Clarify relocation and transition responsibilities.

Dev currently runs two treatment sites, earns $145k, and would relocate after the school term in December. They can commute in blocks before then. They need enough decision authority to be accountable for outages and a documented trigger for the director title. Temporary reduced base is possible with lodging and a guaranteed increase. Work out dates, accountability and the fallback if succession slips.

title: Research editor appointment at Finch Review
context: Finch Review wants Noor to establish a methods desk. An editorial project Noor already directs will run for another nine months. Both sides are willing to design an unusual appointment.
private: Noor can give three days per week until March, four afterward. An outside project must continue independently; its data and unfinished articles cannot be assigned to Finch. Noor wants final say over methods corrections and $125k annualized at full time. Flexible on title and a review milestone. Seek a package that addresses conflicts and the move to four days.

You need a desk taking submissions four days a week by December. You can pair Noor with a deputy one day, but only if there is a documented review process. Budget is $118k annualized or $128k with responsibility for training the deputy. The editor-in-chief retains final publication authority. Outside work is acceptable with recusal and separate materials. Decide what happens on disputed corrections.

title: Sharing robotics drawings with a test partner
context: An actuator designer and a testing house must agree how drawings can be used for vibration tests. The draft allows sharing with any adviser, bars all copies and gives the designer audit access on demand. Exchange actual replacement wording where useful.
private: The CAD geometry is sensitive. Named test personnel and equivalent confidentiality terms are essential. You can allow encrypted working copies and limited derivative fixtures if destroyed after acceptance. You need proof of destruction, but could accept independent certification rather than site access. No reuse to develop competing products.

The test house uses a specialist machining shop and an accredited lab, and must keep calibration records for two years. It cannot allow unannounced inspections of a shared customer site. It can isolate drawing extracts, attest to deletion and keep records without geometry. It needs a way to substitute a specialist during the job. Negotiate the attachments and verification.

title: Festival preview and embargo for an unfinished film
context: A festival is considering an unfinished film. The draft forbids any copying and any disclosure until public release. Agree a review and publicity workflow or explain which approvals remain.
private: Four programmers and an outside accessibility reviewer need access. Two use offline screeners on encrypted equipment. The selection board must be able to hear a short synopsis. You need permission to draft the catalog if selected, but can promise no publication until announcement. The screener platform retains a backup for 30 days.

The producer has promised a financier that the ending and cast cameo will stay secret. The rights holder can accept named reviewing staff and watermarking; offline copies require a deletion record. The producer wants to approve publicity excerpts, can clear draft copy within two business days and may need to withdraw a cut suddenly. Work through embargo trigger, withdrawal and backups.

title: Field-trial data and incident reporting
context: A sensor maker is offering a trial at three transit depots. A draft NDA calls all measurements confidential and requires approval before any disclosure. Negotiate a text both project teams can operate under.
private: Keep raw failure traces and firmware parameters restricted to the trial team. You want 10 working days to review external reports and rights to publish aggregate uptime without route or depot identifiers. You can accept an urgent safety exception with later notice. Determine whether an external maintenance contractor needs the raw data.

Your safety lead must notify authorities promptly about serious incidents and cannot promise prior clearance. A maintenance contractor needs enough diagnostic detail to repair a device. The transit board wants monthly aggregate results. Exact depot/time pairs can identify employees. Agree the routine reporting workflow, urgent exceptions and who approves publication.

title: Unreleased donor materials in a digitization trial
context: An archive and a scanning studio are reviewing a confidentiality schedule for a pilot involving unpublished donor letters. The draft says subcontractors may process materials, files may be retained for quality control, and publicity requires written consent.
private: The studio uses an external color specialist for the first batch. Master images are more useful than crops for color calibration; offer an alternative if rejected. You need ten days to correct scans, backups rotate after 45 days, and the studio wants to publish an anonymized process image. Offer a specific access and deletion schedule.

Two donor collections prohibit third-party viewing of handwriting and identifying content. You can provide a calibration sheet and allow approved specialists to see masked images from other collections. You need a short retention period, an incident contact and evidence of deletion. You might permit a photograph of equipment only after written approval. Agree what goes in the signed schedule and flag any outstanding exception.
